# `pmxhelpr` v0.8.0 is live!

A new version of `pmxhelpr` is now available! This post covers what has changed
since `0.5.x`: two new feature sets in `0.6.0` and `0.7.0`, and intenral updates
and consistent argument names in `0.8.0`.

## 0.6.0 - Plot styling with `ggstylekit`

Plot styling is now powered by the `ggstylekit` package, replacing the
`pmx_*` element/theme system introduced in `0.5.0`.

* Plot aesthetics are controlled with `ggstylekit::style_spec()` using the
 `style` argument (replaces `theme`). 
* `reveal()`, `combine_styled_plots()`, and `legend_spec()` are re-exported

**Versions `0.5.x`**

```{r theme}
#| eval: false
plot_dvtime(data_sad_pk, dosenorm = TRUE, 
            theme = plot_dvtime_theme(obs_point = pmx_point(alpha = 0)))
```

**Version `0.6.0` and higher**

```{r style}
#| warning: false
plot_alpha <- plot_dvtime(data_sad_pk, dosenorm = TRUE,
                          style = style_dvtime(alphas = c(obs_point = 0)))
```

***Note***: as of `0.7.0` the entire observed data point layer can be removed 
instead of hidden with `show_obs = FALSE`

```{r show_obs}
#| warning: false
plot_show <- plot_dvtime(data_sad_pk, dosenorm = T, show_obs = FALSE) 
```

```{r, plot-layout}
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2
plot_alpha + plot_show
```

The different x-axis labels and limits result from the differential handling of
the observed data point layer, hidden with alpha on the left and removed on 
the right.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# 0.7.0 - Forest plot workflow

A forest plot workflow was introduced in version `0.7.0` for  test-to-reference 
comparisons of exposure or response. The design mirrors the dose-proportionality
and VPC toolchains, with summary and dual mode plotting functions. 

  + `plot_forest()`: dual mode plotting function for forest plots for 
  test-to-reference comparisons, such as covariate impact assessment. 
  + `df_forest()`: summary function to derive forest plot statistics from a
  pre-processed simulation replicates, returns a `forest_stats` object
  + `df_forest_preprocess()`: pre-processing function for simulation outputs

```{r forest-plot}
plot_forest(data_sad_pkforest, metric = "AUCRATIO", 
            ref_band = c(0.8, 1.25))+ 
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(0.75, 3), breaks = c(0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

# 0.8.0 - Consistent argument names

Replicate and model-output arguments are renamed to match the other `*_var`
column arguments. The old names still work with a deprecation warning.

**Versions `0.7.x`**

```{r deprecated}
#| eval: false
df_mrgsim_replicate(data, model, replicates = 100, irep_name = "SIM",
                    ipred_var = "IPRED", sim_dv_var = "DV")
```

**Version `0.8.0` and higher**

```{r renamed}
#| eval: false
df_mrgsim_replicate(data, model, replicates = 100, rep_var = "SIM",
                    ipred_output = "IPRED", dv_output = "DV")
```

  + `irep_name` → `rep_var` in `df_mrgsim_replicate()`, `df_vpcstats()`,
  `plot_vpc_cont()`, `plot_vpc_cens()`, and `df_forest_preprocess()`
  + `output_var` → `ipred_output` in `df_mrgsim_addpred()`
  + Arguments after `ntime_var` in `df_mrgsim_replicate()` moved, so pass
  them by name

Also in `0.8.0`:

  + `reveal()` now works on VPC plots
  + `validate_pmx_stats()` checks a stats container against its full contract
  + `plot_vpc_legend(stats = )` takes `ci`, `pi`, and `loq` from a
  `df_vpcstats()` result

## Installation

It is recommended that all users upgrade to `pmxhelpr` 0.8.0 and `ggstylekit` 
0.4.1 from their PRISM repositories (`rv` recommended).

The recommended way to install pmxhelpr is with [rv](https://github.com/A2-ai/rv).
Add the following to your project's `rproject.toml`, then run `rv sync`:

``` toml
repositories = [
    { alias = "CRAN", 
      url = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest" },
    { alias = "pmxhelpr", 
      url = "https://prism.dev.a2-ai.cloud/rpkgs/pmxhelpr/0.8.0/" },
    { alias = "ggstylekit", 
      url = "https://prism.dev.a2-ai.cloud/rpkgs/ggstylekit/0.4.1/" }
]

dependencies = [
    "pmxhelpr"
]
```

For more information, see the package website: 
https://ryancrass.github.io/pmxhelpr/
